Nearly two years after President Donald Trump took office, Agriculture Secretary Brooke Rollins continues to place the blame for exorbitant grocery prices on his predecessor, former President Joe Biden.

Appearing on Newsmax this week, Rollins was asked about the Trump administration’s message to Americans who are experiencing a significant strain on their wallets as the holiday season gets underway.

“As we all know, in the Biden administration, the price of groceries, inflation averaged about 20% increase, the highest we had ever seen [in] 2022, 2023,” she said. “We are back down to normal levels of inflation for food, between 2.5 to 3%. So the good news is we’ve gotten it under control, and now the work to continue to decrease prices — make sure we’re protecting our farmers, right? But continue to decrease prices — will continue.”

“Turkey itself is about 15% lower than it was in 2022, when it hit an all-time high. So we’re moving in the right direction,” Rollins continued. “But listen, gas and fuel really drives everything ... as we see the cost of gas and diesel come down, the prices of groceries will continue to track behind that, so we should see some relief very, very soon.”

Moments later, Rollins echoed Trump’s recent remarks by pointing out that a recent dip in gas prices took place only after the midterm elections, which saw the Democratic Party take control of both chambers of Congress.

“Isn’t that interesting, as soon as the election’s over, the price begins to move significantly back in the right direction?” she said.

According to Fortune, the average price of gas in the U.S. has dropped about 90 cents a gallon, the lowest level since March.

Still, gas prices remain higher than last year and are expected to significantly impact holiday season travel. GasBuddy estimates shared by CNN Tuesday found that Americans are expected to spend $980 million more on travel this Thanksgiving break than they did over the same five-day period in 2025.

Rollins, like other members of the Trump administration, has been quick to publicly shift criticism of the high cost of living and other consequences of Trump’s policies onto Biden.

Ahead of the midterms, many farmers cited Trump’s trade war and his administration’s tariffs on Canadian goods for higher production costs and export uncertainty. In an appearance on Fox News this month, however, Rollins called the “four years of terrible policies under Joe Biden” the main driver of costs, adding: “We’re digging ourselves out of that, but I think we’re finally there.”
